questions.text: What is this part for? The 16 × 8 × 22 mm block with a 1.87 mm section could be a clip, a spacer, a stand, or a display piece. It drives wall count and infill at that thin section.

options.label: Functional (clip, hook, or latch)
options.impact: Strength: 3 walls (1.2 mm) carry the 1.87 mm section; 40% infill fills the remaining 0.67 mm channel solid enough for the bridge to grip under load.

options.label: General structural (spacer, stand, or small bracket)
options.impact: Strength: 3 walls move most of the part's resistance into the periphery where the 1.87 mm cross-section is thinnest; 30% infill keeps it light without a hollow core.
options.why: The 1.87 mm section is this part's constraint. At 2 walls the infill channel is barely 1 mm wide — 3 walls make the periphery do the work, which is where a thin block actually resists bending.

options.label: Decorative or display
options.impact: Surface: 2 walls give a clean outer face; risk: at 0.8 mm of wall the part is flimsy to handle, and the 1.07 mm infill channel is too narrow for the infill to bond well to both walls.

questions.text: The 10 mm² face at 90° is a true ceiling. The preset has enable_support=0, but even a short span will droop in PLA at 90° without something beneath it. Support it or let it bridge?

options.label: Tree support under the bridge
options.impact: Surface: the face prints flat against a small tree; risk: minimal — 10 mm² means a few branches, easy to snap off.
options.why: At 90° the face is pointing straight down. PLA has no time to stiffen before the next layer lands on a sagging string; a tree under 10 mm² is the smallest possible support and the safest way to keep the bridge flat.

options.label: No support — bridge with cooling
options.impact: Surface: clean underside if the span is ≤ 3 mm; risk: past that, the bridge sags, the first layer pulls off, and the face is pitted.

options.label: Design note — chamfer the face to 45° in CAD
options.impact: Strength: a 45° chamfer is inherently stronger than a 90° ledge and needs no support; but it changes the model, so it's a design call, not a print setting.
